entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Gaius Sulpicius Gallus or Galus was a general, statesman and orator of the Roman Republic. In 169 BC, he served as praetor urbanus. Under Lucius Aemilius Paulus, his intimate friend, he commanded the 2nd legion in the campaign against Perseus, king of Macedonia, and gained great reputation for having predicted a lunar eclipse on the night before the Battle of Pydna. On his return from Macedonia he was elected consul, and in the same year reduced the Ligurians to submission. In 164 BC he was sent as ambassador to Greece and Asia, where he held a meeting at Sardis to investigate the charges brought against Eumenes II of Pergamon by the representatives of various cities of Asia Minor.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gaius Sulpicius Gallus played a crucial role in the campaign against Perseus of Macedonia and was elected consul in the same year. His reputation as a skilled orator and military commander earned him significant regional influence.
